title: Catholic Reformation (Council of Trent and the Jesuits)
summary: The Catholic Reformation, long called the Counter-Reformation, was a revival of the Roman Catholic Church in answer to the Protestant Reformation. Ignatius of Loyola’s Jesuits led it, and missionaries such as Francis Xavier carried it overseas. The Council of Trent, opened under Pope Paul III on 13 December 1545 and closed on 4 December 1563, defined doctrine and issued disciplinary decrees; reforming popes followed with a new Roman Breviary (1568) and Missal (1570). The Catholic Encyclopedia dates the period of revival to 1648.

uncertainty.note: Council of Trent met from 1545 to 1563; the broader Counter-Reformation revival is traditionally dated through the end of the Thirty Years' War in 1648.
